requirements_origin: Development builds use fresh fixtures. Public experimental previews are not compatibility baselines; stable release baselines must be explicitly declared.

test_framework.name: XADBTest
test_framework.historical_cases_usage: Design lessons only; write new tests and independent expectations from XADB contracts

version_policy.stable_contract_from: first explicitly declared stable XADB release
version_policy.compatibility_domain: every earlier stable release in the same XADB major; experimental development snapshots are excluded
version_policy.direction: older producer or client -> newer consumer or server
version_policy.sql_and_public_error_semantics: newer release preserves previously specified public behavior; documented bug fixes preserve intended contract, not historical wrong answers
version_policy.old_data_catalog_wal_to_new_engine: read, recover, optionally convert, then continue read/write without loss of acknowledged commits or logical semantics
version_policy.old_binary_on_unsupported_new_format: reject before modifying database; this is a defensive guard, not successful reverse compatibility
version_policy.format_envelope: explicit format/generation identifiers during development; customer-visible compatibility envelope fixed from first declared stable release
version_policy.conversion_strategy_initial: offline shadow generation with retained recovery source, resumable journal, validated state, and durable manifest publication
version_policy.conversion_fault_invariant: new engine selects a complete recoverable old or new generation, never a mixture; acknowledged transactions and prior semantics remain intact
version_policy.original_reclamation: only after durable selection and verified recoverability of the new generation
version_policy.pre_upgrade_backup_restore: separate recovery point; does not preserve later acknowledged writes and is not a lossless downgrade
version_policy.major_breaking_changes: separate explicit design when prior public semantics or prior-data processing cannot be preserved; changing internal format alone does not require a major

required_release_evidence: old client to new server with previously specified semantics
old data and catalog to new reader or converter, then new writes and checkpoint
old WAL after crash to new recovery, preserving acknowledged commits and batch atomicity
old same-major backup to new restore with independent semantic and integrity oracles
all earlier same-major minor sources to candidate, including skipped-minor upgrades without intermediate server installation
crash cuts before and after conversion manifest publication, restart with new engine, and repeated conversion safety
new writes after conversion survive crash and recovery with the new engine
unsupported-format old-reader guard rejects without modification; does not require old reader to open converted data
stable disk releases: preserve declared data/WAL/backup formats, row/index/catalog identities and uniqueness within the published compatibility baseline
not_claimed: Any XADB product release exists or was tested here
An old binary understands a newer persistent format or preserves post-upgrade writes on downgrade
Sampled version pairs prove every patch/configuration combination
Backward compatibility alone supports mixed-minor replication or zero-downtime rolling upgrades

pair_count_model.indices: n stable-release minors within one major, ordered by release; internal distributions excluded; patch and fault variants counted separately

internal_distribution_policy.unsupported_existing_format: reject explicitly; no implicit deletion or overwrite

required_release_evidence_applicability: customer delivery only; previous versions mean stable-release baselines, never internal builds. No prior customer baseline is N/A, not PASS. Current-build correctness, recovery and independent oracle checks remain mandatory for internal work.
superseded_policy: The earlier rule making official internal distributions compatibility baselines is superseded by the user-confirmed no-compatibility default. Historical validation.json retains its original design-review record and is not current policy.
legacy_product_migration_scope: Logical schema/data/workload mapping, import/export and validation are required replacement capabilities (R14); no legacy physical file reader or wire/binary compatibility is implied.
